newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Sibekobank to get Novosibirskenergo shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian Sibekobank to get Novosibirskenergo shares.

text.p: Russia's Novosibirsk regional administration plans to put its 36 percent voting share stake in Novosibirskenergo power utility in trust with local Sibekobank, a Novosibirsk official said on Thursday.
"We have a preliminary agreement with Sibekobank and they are finialising it," First Deputy Head Vasily Kiselyov told Reuters. "Soon we will have a legally-approved, three-year agreement."
He said Sibekobank would provide guarantees to investors in the regional administration's 300 billion rouble ($51.94 million) KODO municipal bond programme in exchange for the shares in trust.
The bank in principle could sell the shares if Novosibirsk defaulted on the bonds.
"Novosibirskenergo shares are liquid and so can be regarded as a guarantee to the bank for possible investment in the KODO market," said a Sibekobank official.
Kiselyov said the administration planned an independent audit of Novosibirskenergo and to work out a programme to improve the company's finances.
He said after Novosibirskenergo shares were placed in trust the admistration would work out new possibilities of electricity supply to the region.
"Maybe it will be cheaper for us to buy electricity in other regions than to build new heat power stations," he said.
The bank official said he expected revenues would improve significantly for the utility.
"We want to increase our profits from holding the shares," he said.
"In 1994-95 the regional administration received 1.7 billion roubles in dividends. That is tiny. We would like to receive reliable money, in a volume much bigger than these dividends."

In 1996 Novosibirskenergo's accounts payable amounted to 2 trillion roubles, accounts receivable were 1.77 trillion roubles. Net profit was 981.49 billion roubles, pre-tax profit was 239.57 billion roubles.
